discovery: A bispecific antibody that substitutes for factor VIII activity in hemophilia A
credited_names: Kunihiro Hattori; Takehisa Kitazawa; Tomoyuki Igawa
scientific_basis: Emicizumab bridges coagulation factors IX and X to compensate for deficient factor VIII activity.
rationale: A specific engineering invention with a clear clinical mechanism and substantial treatment benefit.
main_reservation: Could be viewed as a powerful disease-specific invention rather than a broad physiological discovery.
attribution_note: The 2026 Lasker supports this three-person pool; the citation should focus on factor-mimetic bispecific engineering rather than all antibody therapeutics.

discovery: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids for studying tissue biology and disease
credited_names: Hans Clevers; Toshiro Sato
scientific_basis: Single intestinal stem cells can generate self-organizing organoids, enabling long-term culture of tissue-like structures.
rationale: Changed experimental access to normal and diseased human tissues through a concrete biological discovery and culture method.
main_reservation: Clinical impact and physiological completeness vary; adult stem-cell organoids should be distinguished from pluripotent stem-cell organoids.
attribution_note: This narrow scope supports Clevers and Sato; a broader organoid citation would require additional pioneers and separate attribution research.

discovery: BCR-ABL inhibition and molecularly targeted treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia
credited_names: Brian J. Druker; Charles L. Sawyers; Nicholas B. Lydon
scientific_basis: Imatinib targets the BCR-ABL kinase driving CML; investigation of resistance enabled subsequent targeted inhibitors.
rationale: A durable demonstration that targeting an oncogenic driver can transform cancer treatment.
main_reservation: Broader precision-oncology claims overlap with HER2 therapy and depend on many earlier discoveries.
attribution_note: Keep this kinase-inhibitor achievement separate from trastuzumab; any combined award must still fit the total three-person limit.

discovery: Biomolecular condensates and phase separation in cellular organization
credited_names: Anthony A. Hyman; Clifford P. Brangwynne; Dirk Görlich; Steven L. McKnight
scientific_basis: Phase separation and interactions of low-complexity protein domains explain important forms of cellular organization without membrane boundaries.
rationale: Introduced a physical mechanism for organizing cellular reactions, with experimental work from complementary approaches.
main_reservation: Some proposed functions remain contested or context-dependent; liquid behavior, hydrogels and aggregation should not be equated.
attribution_note: Hyman-Brangwynne and Gorlich-McKnight support different emphases; select a precise achievement and at most three researchers during deliberation.

discovery: CFTR functional rescue and modulator therapies for cystic fibrosis
credited_names: Fred Van Goor; Jesús Tito González; Michael J. Welsh; Paul A. Negulescu; Sabine Hadida
scientific_basis: Understanding CFTR dysfunction enabled drugs that improve mutant protein folding, trafficking and channel activity.
rationale: A mature example of treating a genetic disease by rescuing the defective protein mechanism.
main_reservation: The mechanistic, screening and medicinal-chemistry contributions are distributed among more than three scientists.
attribution_note: The 2025 Lasker names Welsh, Negulescu and Gonzalez; its scientific account also credits Van Goor and Hadida, retained as alternatives.

discovery: Chaperonin-assisted protein folding
subfield: Molecular cell biology and protein biochemistry
credited_names: Arthur L. Horwich; F. Ulrich Hartl
scientific_basis: Chaperonins provide a protected environment in which proteins can fold, establishing active cellular assistance to protein folding.
rationale: Changed a basic account of how functional proteins arise in cells; attribution is comparatively compact.
main_reservation: Could compete with the unfolded protein response; the committee must distinguish assisted folding from structure prediction.
attribution_note: This is experimental chaperonin biology, distinct from AlphaFold and computational protein design recognized by Chemistry in 2024.

discovery: DNA methylation as a mechanism regulating gene expression
credited_names: Adrian P. Bird; Howard Cedar; Rudolf Jaenisch
scientific_basis: DNA methylation and its recognition influence gene activity; causal experiments connect methylation changes to disease mechanisms.
rationale: A fundamental account of stable gene regulation beyond DNA sequence, supported by mechanistic experiments.
main_reservation: Different discoveries under the broad epigenetics label should not be treated as a single undifferentiated achievement.
attribution_note: Bird and Cedar anchor methylation and expression; Jaenisch represents causal mammalian experiments. Imprinting remains a separate candidate.

discovery: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells for treating cancer
credited_names: Carl H. June; Michel Sadelain
scientific_basis: Engineering T-cell receptors and signaling enabled patient T cells to attack blood cancers, with durable remissions in some patients.
rationale: A mature clinical transformation built on a distinct engineering advance, with an intelligible two-person configuration.
main_reservation: Durability, toxicities and limited solid-tumor success constrain generalization; earlier invention credit must be acknowledged.
attribution_note: June and Sadelain are the proposed living attribution pool for this scope. Eshhar remains essential historical credit but died in 2025.

discovery: GLP-1 physiology and the development of incretin therapies for diabetes and obesity
credited_names: Daniel J. Drucker; Jens Juul Holst; Joel F. Habener; Lotte Bjerre Knudsen; Svetlana Mojsov
scientific_basis: Discovery of active GLP-1 and its insulin-stimulating physiology enabled development of durable therapeutic analogues.
rationale: Combines a defined physiological discovery with major demonstrated clinical benefit; the scientific and therapeutic narratives both support consideration.
main_reservation: Five substantial attribution claims compete for at most three laureate places; citation scope could determine the outcome.
attribution_note: Retain all five. Discovery-focused and drug-development-focused configurations differ; do not silently freeze the older Habener-Holst-Drucker trio.

discovery: HER2-directed antibody therapy for breast cancer
credited_names: Axel Ullrich; Dennis J. Slamon; H. Michael Shepard
scientific_basis: HER2 biology, antibody engineering and clinical development produced trastuzumab for HER2-positive breast cancer.
rationale: A mature, specific route from molecular disease classification to survival-improving treatment.
main_reservation: A combined targeted-cancer-therapy citation would create severe competition for laureate places.
attribution_note: Keep the HER2 antibody development pool intact and separate from the BCR-ABL kinase-inhibitor pool.

discovery: Identification of CFTR as the gene responsible for cystic fibrosis
credited_names: Francis S. Collins; John R. Riordan; Lap-Chee Tsui
scientific_basis: Positional cloning and characterization identified CFTR and connected its disruption to cystic fibrosis.
rationale: A landmark demonstration of finding a disease gene from inheritance and chromosome position.
main_reservation: The original gene discovery and later functional rescue therapies offer competing citation scopes.
attribution_note: Keep gene discovery separate from the Welsh-Negulescu-Gonzalez therapeutic candidate; do not conflate source credit with drug-development credit.

discovery: IL-6 signaling and therapeutic blockade of the IL-6 receptor
credited_names: Tadamitsu Kishimoto; Toshio Hirano
scientific_basis: Discovery and characterization of IL-6 and its signaling system enabled receptor-blocking treatment such as tocilizumab.
rationale: A coherent molecular-to-clinical story with complementary mechanistic contributions and established treatment relevance.
main_reservation: A broad cytokine-therapy award risks conflating this discovery with anti-TNF or IL-1 biology.
attribution_note: The 2011 Japan Prize supports this two-person pool; retain a distinct IL-6 citation.

discovery: Integrins as receptors mediating cell-matrix and cell-cell adhesion
credited_names: Erkki Ruoslahti; Richard O. Hynes; Timothy A. Springer
scientific_basis: Separate discoveries of extracellular matrix and leukocyte adhesion receptors converged on the integrin family.
rationale: A general organizing principle of tissues and immunity with mature evidence and a coherent three-person configuration.
main_reservation: The field is broad; an award needs a sharply defined receptor discovery rather than a general adhesion citation.
attribution_note: Retain both extracellular matrix and immune adhesion origins when evaluating the common molecular family.

discovery: Kinetic stabilization of transthyretin and treatment of amyloid disease
credited_names: Jeffery W. Kelly
scientific_basis: Stabilizing the transthyretin tetramer with tafamidis reduces its dissociation and aggregation and slows disease progression.
rationale: A precise, experimentally grounded connection between protein mechanism and effective disease-modifying therapy.
main_reservation: A narrow disease-focused achievement may compete with broader proteostasis principles; drug-development attribution needs scrutiny.
attribution_note: Kelly anchors the mechanism-and-therapy discovery; avoid claiming that tafamidis demonstrates a universal treatment for all amyloid diseases.

discovery: Leptin and endocrine regulation of appetite and body weight
credited_names: Jeffrey M. Friedman
scientific_basis: Identification of leptin established an endocrine signal linking adipose tissue to feeding behavior and body-weight regulation.
rationale: A fundamental physiological discovery that changed the biological understanding of obesity.
main_reservation: The clinical replacement-therapy story is narrower than that for incretin drugs; this is a distinct mechanism, not a GLP-1 variant.
attribution_note: Friedman is the living pool for this discovery-centered entry; Coleman is indispensable historical credit but died in 2014.

discovery: Long-term potentiation and the synaptic basis of learning and memory
credited_names: Graham L. Collingridge; Richard G. M. Morris; Timothy V. P. Bliss
scientific_basis: Experiments linked persistent strengthening of hippocampal synapses and its molecular mechanisms to spatial learning and memory.
rationale: Combines fundamental physiology with causal investigation of a central brain function.
main_reservation: A new citation must make clear its distinction from earlier Nobel-recognized work on memory and from place-cell discoveries.
attribution_note: Use the established 2016 Brain Prize pool while recognizing that LTP and memory are not interchangeable in every experimental context.

discovery: Mammalian genomic imprinting and parent-of-origin gene expression
credited_names: Davor Solter; M. Azim Surani
scientific_basis: Independent embryo experiments established functional nonequivalence of maternal and paternal genomes and the basis of genomic imprinting.
rationale: An unexpected, fundamental discovery with direct consequences for development and human genetic disorders.
main_reservation: Its relation to DNA methylation can invite overbroad merging; the original developmental discovery should remain identifiable.
attribution_note: Keep the independent Surani and Solter discoveries together, while distinguishing later molecular imprint maintenance mechanisms.

discovery: Massively parallel DNA sequencing for genome-scale biology and medicine
credited_names: David Klenerman; Pascal Mayer; Shankar Balasubramanian
scientific_basis: Scalable massively parallel sequencing made DNA sequence analysis broadly usable in biomedical research and medicine.
rationale: An enabling invention with exceptional effects on genetics, diagnostics and experimental biology.
main_reservation: The invention is also a plausible Chemistry achievement; alternative sequencing platforms have separate priority histories.
attribution_note: This is the specific pool recognized by the 2022 Breakthrough Prize. Do not conflate it with every next-generation or long-read sequencing platform.

discovery: Notch signaling as a mechanism of cell-fate specification
credited_names: Gary Struhl; Iva Greenwald; Spyros Artavanis-Tsakonas
scientific_basis: Genetic and molecular discoveries established how Notch signaling controls cell fate, development and tissue patterning.
rationale: A conserved biological mechanism with foundational experimental support and continuing relevance to tissue biology.
main_reservation: Cell-fate specification has many historical contributors, and the precise discovery boundary matters.
attribution_note: These are the three researchers jointly recognized by Gairdner in 2025; this pool is a defensible starting point rather than exhaustive historical credit.

discovery: Optical coherence tomography for noninvasive tissue imaging
credited_names: David Huang; Eric A. Swanson; James G. Fujimoto
scientific_basis: Optical coherence tomography produces depth-resolved cross-sectional images of tissue and transformed retinal examination.
rationale: A mature invention with extensive direct medical use and a compact attribution configuration.
main_reservation: Its optics foundation could also support consideration in Physics; Medicine requires a convincing clinical-invention framing.
attribution_note: Use the imaging-invention trio; keep OCT distinct from the separate VEGF discovery even though both transformed retinal care.

discovery: Optogenetic control of genetically specified cells with light
credited_names: Edward S. Boyden; Ernst Bamberg; Georg Nagel; Gero Miesenböck; Karl Deisseroth; Peter Hegemann
scientific_basis: Light-sensitive microbial proteins and genetic targeting permit experimental activation or inhibition of specified neuronal populations.
rationale: Enabled causal experiments on neural circuits at a scale and specificity that changed neuroscience.
main_reservation: Several independent enabling contributions make a three-person award difficult; tool impact and biological discovery need to be distinguished.
attribution_note: Preserve the six living researchers named by the 2013 Brain Prize. Oesterhelt is historical credit only because he died in 2022.

discovery: Orexin signaling in wakefulness and the cause of narcolepsy
credited_names: Emmanuel Mignot; Masashi Yanagisawa
scientific_basis: Orexin signaling maintains wakefulness, and loss of this system explains narcolepsy; the pathway also supplies drug targets.
rationale: Connects a basic physiological discovery to a defined human disorder and pharmacology, with clear complementary attribution.
main_reservation: Therapeutic maturity differs between receptor antagonism for insomnia and receptor agonism for narcolepsy.
attribution_note: Treat discovery of the pathway and explanation of disease as complementary work. The 2026 Lasker recognizes these contributions.

discovery: PCSK9 and human genetic validation of a cholesterol-lowering therapeutic target
credited_names: Catherine Boileau; Helen H. Hobbs; Jonathan C. Cohen; Marianne Abifadel; Nabil G. Seidah
scientific_basis: PCSK9 disease mutations and protective loss-of-function variants established a target for reducing LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular risk.
rationale: A strong example of human genetics directing therapeutic development, with clear physiological consequences.
main_reservation: Several discovery and validation teams compete for the three-person limit; distinction from earlier LDL-receptor recognition is necessary.
attribution_note: Retain protein discovery, disease genetics and protective-variant teams; a Hobbs-Cohen-only framing would prematurely exclude foundational work.

discovery: Single-cell RNA sequencing for resolving cellular identity and heterogeneity
credited_names: Aviv Regev; Evan Z. Macosko; Fuchou Tang; Rickard Sandberg; Sten Linnarsson; Stephen R. Quake; Steven A. McCarroll
scientific_basis: Single-cell transcriptome profiling, sensitive full-length protocols and droplet methods enabled molecular analysis of heterogeneous cell populations.
rationale: Opened a major experimental view of cell identity, with wide use across physiology, development and disease.
main_reservation: The first demonstration, improved sensitivity, high throughput and atlas applications represent distinct credit claims; the three-person constraint is severe.
attribution_note: Preserve methodological alternatives. Inclusion of Sandberg and Linnarsson creates direct conflicts for the existing simulated committee; these require an explicit protocol choice.

discovery: Spatial transcriptomics for mapping gene expression within intact tissue
credited_names: Joakim Lundeberg; Jonas Frisén; Patrik L. Ståhl; Xiaowei Zhuang
scientific_basis: Spatially resolved sequencing and multiplexed RNA imaging associate molecular cell identity with tissue position.
rationale: Restores anatomical context to molecular cell analysis and enables detailed investigation of tissue organization.
main_reservation: Distinct sequencing and imaging inventions have separate priorities, and application maturity varies.
attribution_note: Zhuang anchors MERFISH; Lundeberg, Frisen and Stahl anchor the spatial sequencing approach. Linnarsson coauthored the original spatial-transcriptomics paper.

discovery: The BRCA1 locus and the genetic basis of inherited breast cancer
credited_names: Mary-Claire King
scientific_basis: Family-based genetic analysis established the BRCA1 locus and a major inherited component of breast cancer susceptibility.
rationale: An identifiable discovery changed disease risk assessment and preventive medicine.
main_reservation: Mapping the locus, cloning BRCA1, identifying BRCA2 and exploiting DNA-repair vulnerabilities are different achievements.
attribution_note: King is the pool for this deliberately narrow citation. A broader BRCA1/BRCA2 citation requires additional names and evidence at the merge stage.

discovery: The cGAS-STING pathway linking cytosolic DNA sensing to innate immunity
credited_names: Glen N. Barber; Hiroki Ishikawa; Jiaxi Wu; Lijun Sun; Zhijian James Chen
scientific_basis: STING is an innate immune signaling adaptor; cGAS detects cytosolic DNA and produces the cyclic messenger cGAMP.
rationale: A clearly defined mechanism with consequences for infection, inflammation and antitumor immunity.
main_reservation: The clinical translational story is less mature than the mechanistic discovery, and a broad citation complicates credit.
attribution_note: A cGAS-centered citation could emphasize Chen and the original biochemical discoverers; a pathway citation also brings STING discovery into scope.

discovery: The unfolded protein response and signaling from the endoplasmic reticulum
credited_names: Kazutoshi Mori; Peter Walter
scientific_basis: Identification of ER stress signaling machinery explained how cells sense misfolded proteins and increase their folding capacity.
rationale: A fundamental, widely reproduced cellular mechanism with an unusually clear two-person attribution.
main_reservation: Direct therapeutic benefit is less prominent than its biological importance; related proteostasis discoveries are separate candidates.
attribution_note: Keep ER stress sensing and signaling separate from chaperonin-assisted folding and from therapeutic stabilization of transthyretin.

discovery: TNF blockade as a treatment for rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory disease
credited_names: Marc Feldmann; Ravinder N. Maini
scientific_basis: Experimental work identified TNF as an actionable inflammatory driver and clinical studies established effective TNF blockade.
rationale: A compelling mechanism-to-treatment story with established benefit and clear complementary laboratory and clinical roles.
main_reservation: The previous Medicine prize addressed immune tolerance; thematic succession is a forecasting consideration, not an exclusion rule.
attribution_note: Retain this cytokine-blockade discovery independently of IL-6 and the already rewarded regulatory T-cell story.

discovery: TOR signaling as a regulator of cell growth and nutrient responses
credited_names: David M. Sabatini; Michael N. Hall; Stuart L. Schreiber
scientific_basis: TOR proteins couple nutrient availability to cell growth; mammalian TOR signaling extends this mechanism to physiological regulation.
rationale: A central conserved mechanism with effects across metabolism, growth and disease.
main_reservation: Discovery of yeast TOR, mammalian mTOR and later pathway mechanisms support different attribution boundaries.
attribution_note: Hall, Sabatini and Schreiber are an attribution pool, not an endorsed mandatory trio; distinguish original target discovery from later mechanistic work.

discovery: VEGF biology and inhibition of pathological angiogenesis
credited_names: Donald R. Senger; Harold F. Dvorak; Napoleone Ferrara
scientific_basis: VEGF and vascular permeability factor proved to be the same signaling molecule; blocking VEGF enabled anti-angiogenic treatment.
rationale: Connects a defined biological pathway to mature clinical benefit, particularly in retinal disease.
main_reservation: Discovery of permeability activity, molecular identification and therapeutic development support different credit allocations.
attribution_note: Ferrara is central to a therapeutic citation; Dvorak and Senger become important for a broader discovery-of-VEGF/VPF citation.

discovery: Virus-like particle vaccines that prevent HPV infection and related cancers
credited_names: Douglas R. Lowy; Ian H. Frazer; John T. Schiller
scientific_basis: Noninfectious papillomavirus-like particles can induce protective immunity and form the basis of vaccines preventing HPV infection.
rationale: Links a precise technological advance to cancer prevention and substantial public-health benefit.
main_reservation: Particle design, immunogenicity and vaccine development have overlapping priority histories.
attribution_note: Retain Lowy, Schiller and Frazer for committee attribution review; the Lasker account describes both the NCI work and Frazer contribution.
